drills.q: Why does DDP's ring all-reduce communication cost not grow proportionally with the number of GPUs?
drills.a: Total data moved per GPU is 2*(N-1)/N * S. As N grows, (N-1)/N approaches 1, so bandwidth cost approaches a constant independent of GPU count -- only the smaller latency term scales with N.

drills.q: What is DDP's actual scaling ceiling, if not communication cost?
drills.a: The full model, gradients, and optimizer state must fit on every single GPU, since DDP replicates rather than shards model state -- adding more GPUs doesn't reduce any one GPU's memory footprint.

drills.q: Walk through the memory arithmetic for ZeRO Stage 1 vs Stage 3 using Psi=7.5B params, Nd=64 GPUs.
drills.a: 16*Psi bytes total (2Psi fp16 params + 2Psi fp16 grads + 4Psi fp32 master + 4Psi momentum + 4Psi variance) = 120GB baseline. Stage1: 4Psi+12Psi/64 = 31.4GB. Stage3: 16Psi/64 = 1.875GB, a 64x reduction.

drills.q: Why does ZeRO Stage 3 need roughly 1.5x plain DDP's communication volume?
drills.a: Parameters are never held in full on any GPU, so each layer's shard must be all-gathered into a full copy immediately before both forward and backward compute, then freed -- adding a full parameter all-gather twice on top of DDP's existing gradient all-reduce.

drills.q: What does FSDP2 change relative to FSDP1's sharding, and why does that matter?
drills.a: FSDP2 shards at per-parameter granularity rather than FSDP1's flattened/concatenated sharding, composing more cleanly with mixed dtypes per layer, freezing individual parameters (LoRA-style fine-tuning), and torch.compile -- reported up to ~5x ZeRO-3's throughput where both fit memory.

drills.q: Why is tensor parallelism kept within a single node while pipeline parallelism tolerates cross-node communication better?
drills.a: Tensor parallelism communicates at every split layer -- very high frequency, sensitive to interconnect bandwidth/latency, so it's kept on fast NVLink within one node. Pipeline parallelism only communicates activations/gradients at stage boundaries, far less frequently, tolerating slower inter-node links.

drills.q: Derive the pipeline bubble fraction for 4 stages with 8 microbatches, and explain why increasing microbatch count helps.
drills.a: Bubble fraction ~= (P-1)/M = (4-1)/8 = 37.5% idle. Increasing to M=32 gives (4-1)/32 ~= 9.4% -- the fixed pipeline fill/drain cost gets amortized over more total useful work as M grows.

drills.q: A model doesn't fit even after ZeRO-3/FSDP2 at max affordable GPU count. What's the next lever, and why doesn't more data-parallel sharding help further?
drills.a: Tensor parallelism (split the oversized layer) and/or pipeline parallelism (split model depth). ZeRO/FSDP shards across data-parallel replicas, but a full layer's parameters must still be materialized on one GPU when it computes -- more replicas doesn't shrink that per-layer peak requirement.

drills.q: Why do the largest production training runs combine data, tensor, and pipeline parallelism simultaneously rather than picking one?
drills.a: Each addresses a different ceiling: data parallelism (with ZeRO/FSDP) scales throughput and reduces aggregate memory; tensor parallelism handles a single layer too large for one GPU; pipeline parallelism handles a model whose total depth doesn't fit. No single axis covers every possible ceiling alone.

drills.q: What's the practical difference between ZeRO/FSDP and tensor parallelism, given both reduce per-GPU memory?
drills.a: ZeRO/FSDP reduce aggregate memory across a data-parallel group but still require a full layer's parameters materialized on one GPU at compute time. Tensor parallelism genuinely splits that layer's computation so no GPU ever needs its full parameters -- relevant specifically when one layer alone exceeds a single GPU's capacity.

drills.q: A model fits comfortably on a single GPU but training is too slow. Which distributed strategy first, and why not ZeRO/FSDP by default?
drills.a: Plain DDP -- simplest failure modes, near-N-independent communication cost. ZeRO/FSDP's all-gather sharding overhead is a real cost with no benefit when memory was never the binding constraint; add sharding only once memory pressure actually emerges.

drills.q: Design: choosing the degree of tensor-parallel, pipeline-parallel, and data-parallel GPUs for a large model on a real cluster. What determines each?
drills.a: Tensor-parallel degree sized to fit one layer's compute/memory within one fast-interconnect node (e.g. 8 GPUs on NVLink). Pipeline-parallel degree sized to fit total model depth across available nodes while keeping microbatch count high enough for an acceptable bubble fraction. Data-parallel degree uses remaining GPUs for throughput -- empirically tuned to actual cluster topology, not a fixed formula.
